chunks: That was narrated - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Rahman from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who prays behind an Imam whom he follows. The Imam bowed, and the man made a mistake (sahw) while he was behind him, so he did not bow until the Imam raised his head and lowered himself for prostration. Should he bow and then catch up with the Imam while the people are in their prostration, or what should he do? He said: 'He should bow, then lower himself and complete his prayer with them, and there is nothing upon him.'
And likewise, if he made a mistake and salam (ended prayer) before the Imam, there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.رَفَعَ الْإِمَامُ رَأْسَهُ: The Imam raised his head (from bowing)
key_terms.سَهَا: To make a mistake or forget in prayer
key_terms.فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: And there is nothing upon him (no penalty/compensation required)
key_terms.يَلْحَقُ بِالْإِمَامِ: To catch up with the Imam

ai.seo_question: What should a worshipper do if he misses the Imam's bowing due to a mistake during congregational prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of individual accountability within congregational prayer, ruling that a follower who misses a pillar due to error must complete it independently rather than waiting for the Imam. It further clarifies that premature conclusion of prayer by the follower incurs no penalty, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the follower’s prayer remains valid even if their sequence diverges slightly from the Imam’s. This ruling underscores the flexibility in *sahw* (forgetfulness) mechanics, distinguishing between essential pillars and optional acts in the context of following an Imam.
